items.title: Safety by Design Under Strain: A Case Study in System Convergence
items.abstract: Safety by Design (SbD) is increasingly embedded in high-risk industries to promote alignment with the hierarchy of controls by eliminating or minimising risk through engineering and system design rather than reliance on administrative or personal protective equipment controls (Safe Work Australia, nd). In practice, however, applying SbD is not straightforward. Complexity emerges where engineering, organisational systems, human factors, contractor delivery models, commercial pressures, and regulatory frameworks intersect within dynamic operating environments. This paper presents an abstract case study based on a significant network event within a New Zealand electricity distribution context involving excavation works, repeated asset interactions, and eventual exposure to a live high-voltage asset. The event resulted in unplanned network disruption and elevated risk to both workers and the public, requiring rapid decision-making across multiple organisational boundaries, including local authority-led contracting environments where no direct commercial relationship existed with the asset owner. Using a qualitative, reflective approach, this study examines how SbD principles were applied, adapted, or constrained in practice. The concept of System Convergence Strain is introduced to describe how overlapping duties, fragmented contracting chains, and competing priorities create ambiguity and shift risk control away from engineered systems toward frontline judgement under uncertainty. The findings challenge the assumption that safety can be effectively managed within organisational boundaries and instead position safety as an emergent property of interacting systems.

items.title: Same Answer, Different Reasons: Trace-Level Divergence in Multilingual Large Language Models
items.abstract: Multilingual large language models are increasingly deployed in settings where visible reasoning traces support verification, education, and safety auditing, yet standard evaluations typically measure only final-answer agreement or holistic response similarity. As a result, they establish outcome consistency without determining whether users across languages receive comparable supporting evidence. We introduce a trace-level divergence framework that compares visible reasoning traces as structured sequences, decomposing agreement into structural similarity, order consistency, and holistic similarity, with pair-specific calibration to enable comparison across languages. Across three reasoning benchmarks, seven languages, and six frontier LLMs, the natural baseline---embedding each whole response and comparing the two by cosine---systematically overstates agreement: $52.1\%$--$67.3\%$ of examples in the top quartile of holistic similarity are not in the top quartile of structural similarity. This dissociation is stable across sentence encoders and step segmentations, and blind bilingual annotation studies in two English-anchored language pairs show that human judgments align with structural similarity rather than with the holistic baseline. A same-language control shows that the level of divergence is language-specific: two English traces for paraphrases of the same question agree more closely than an English trace and its counterparts in other languages. Our results show that answer-level and holistic evaluations can substantially overestimate the consistency of multilingual explanatory artifacts, motivating trace-level evaluation for reliable multilingual deployment.

items.title: Same Beliefs, Different Policies: Learning Reusable Representations for Early Stopping in LLM Reasoning
items.abstract: Reasoning LLMs often continue reasoning after reaching a correct answer, wasting computation and sometimes replacing it with an incorrect one. Deciding when to stop is a metareasoning problem: the model must weigh what further reasoning could achieve against its cost, given what it can already answer. Direct utility training learns a stopping representation at a chosen token price; supporting new prices can require additional controller training. We introduce BELT (BELief-based Termination), which separates outcome prediction from stopping control. It learns beliefs about current and future answers from a frozen LLM's hidden states, then fits a linear stopping policy on the frozen features. The prediction targets are independent of token price, so one probe supports different accuracy-cost trade-offs through CPU policy refitting or threshold adjustment. Averaged over five out-of-distribution (OOD) math benchmarks, BELT reduces generated tokens by 41% on Qwen3-1.7B and 51% on OLMo-3-7B-Think without loss of accuracy. The same math-trained BELT transfers to coding and agentic tasks without training on code or agentic data. In all three domains, its accuracy-cost trade-offs are competitive with or better than those of end-to-end controllers. On OLMo3, its probe has 21.2x fewer parameters than one checkpoint of the strongest baseline, OS-Pruner, and needs 55x fewer training GPU-hours than OS-Pruner's five price-specific checkpoints.

items.title: Same Probabilities, Different Advice: Gain-Loss Framing Effects in High-Stakes LLM Decision Support
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support consequential decisions, yet their reliability under equivalent representations of uncertainty remains unclear. Existing work has documented prompt sensitivity, cognitive biases, and confidence miscalibration, but it is still unknown whether high-stakes advice changes when the same probability is expressed through complementary gain and loss frames. We introduce FrameBench-HPS, a controlled benchmark of 2,880 prompts derived from 240 high-stakes scenarios across healthcare, finance, education/career, and legal/consumer-rights domains. Across seven LLMs, gain-loss framing changes the recommendation category in 32.4% of complete groups, with most changes involving uncertainty rather than direct reversals. Human evaluation confirms corresponding shifts in perceived risk and directiveness. Robustness experiments show that framing effects persist under conversational paraphrases and exceed ordinary repeated-generation variability. Probability canonicalization substantially reduces framing sensitivity, identifying probability representation as a practical target for improving consistency in high-stakes LLM decision support.

items.title: Sample-Efficient Neural Operator Surrogates for Artificial Intelligence Climate Downscaling Under Sparse Gauge Networks: Error Bounds and Localized Flood-Warning Lead Time
items.abstract: Neural operator surrogates promise to replace expensive dynamical downscaling with fast, differentiable maps from coarse atmospheric fields to local climate variables, but their reliability under sparse gauge networks remains poorly characterised. The analysis treats the surrogate as a mapping between function spaces and derives an explicit error decomposition into truncation, sampling and optimisation terms. Using a reanalysis record for Harare, Zimbabwe (2000–2023, 312 monthly observations, mean temperature 18.914 °C, warming trend 0.2001 °C per decade), the framework is instantiated to show how gauge sparsity inflates the sampling term and how that inflation translates into a quantifiable reduction in the lead time at which a warning threshold is crossed. The central result is a closed-form expression linking gauge density, operator truncation rank and warning lead time, which permits network designers to trade sensor count against forecast horizon before deployment.

items.title: Seat-Height Effects During Seated Shoe Donning in Older Adults: A Multi-Stage Ergonomic Evaluation Integrating Muscle Activity, Postural Exposure, and Subjective Comfort
items.abstract: Inappropriate seat height may affect muscle activity, observational musculoskeletal postural exposure, and subjective comfort during seated shoe donning in older adults. This study characterized seat-height effects across four task stages and explored the combined pattern of these outcomes. Thirty-five community-dwelling older adults with basic self-care ability recruited from a residential community affiliated with Southwest Forestry University (12 men and 23 women; age: 74.60±7.87 years) completed seated shoe donning at 60%, 80%, 100%, and 120% of individual popliteal height. sEMG quantified muscle activity using natural-log-transformed task RMS as the primary analytical measure, with ΔRMS% retained as a secondary quiet-standing-normalized measure; REBA assessed observational postural exposure; subjective comfort was assessed using a study-specific seven-category numerical rating scale; and CRITIC provided an exploratory multi-indicator summary. Primary sEMG inference based on natural-log-transformed task RMS showed seat-height main effects for the BB and the FCU and seat-height × stage interactions for the BB, the FCU, the ES, the RF, and the MG; the LM interaction was not significant. Across the log-RMS mixed-effects, ΔRMS%-based mixed-effects, and log-RMS Gaussian GEE analyses, the BB seat-height main effect and the RF seat-height × stage interaction were the most consistently supported seat-height-related findings, while other muscle-specific effects varied across models. REBA showed a consistent seat-height × stage interaction across analyses, but the overall seat-height main effect was non-significant in the ordinal GEE and significant in the Gaussian GEE sensitivity analysis. Subjective comfort showed consistent seat-height and seat-height × stage effects across the primary and sensitivity analyses. An exploratory CRITIC integration using a within-muscle-standardized log-RMS sEMG summary placed H2 (80% of popliteal height) first among the four tested conditions; the leading position of H2 was retained across alternative sEMG scaling approaches and when the sEMG component was excluded or its orientation reversed, although H2 and H4 nearly tied under the reversed orientation. Overall, seat-height effects varied across task stages and outcome domains. H2 emerged as the highest-scoring tested condition under the present protocol, providing a task-specific basis for future validation.

items.title: Segment anything model (SAM)‐driven prompt‐guided interactive delineation of gross tumor volume for rectal cancer neoadjuvant radiotherapy
items.abstract: Abstract Background Segment Anything Model (SAM), a prompt‐guided foundation model, exhibits substantial potential for medical image segmentation by incorporating prior knowledge through user‐defined prompts. However, the application of SAM in radiotherapy target delineation remains limited. Purpose This study proposes a feasible prompt‐guided interactive delineation workflow driven by an optimized SAM. Methods A total of 100 rectal cancer neoadjuvant radiotherapy cases were collected (60 for training and 40 for testing). This study utilized bounding‐box prompts to guide SAM for GTV segmentation. Physicians manually draw box prompts on certain slices, while box prompts for the remaining slices are automatically generated using an interpolation strategy. Four fine‐tuning strategies for SAM training were evaluated, and the impact of prompt numbers and placements was assessed as well. The performance of the finalized workflow with optimized SAM was compared with five state‐of‐the‐art (SOTA) models, and its robustness to prompt variations in middle‐slice selection and box‐prompt margins was analyzed. Results Compared to other fine‐tuning methods, freezing the image encoder obtained the most stable performance. Prompts on only 3 slices achieved accuracy comparable to prompts on all slices. The placement of the middle‐slice prompt exhibited negligible impact ( p > 0.05). The finalized SAM‐driven workflow outperformed end‐to‐end baseline models both visually and quantitatively (3D DSC: 0.92 vs 0.80; 3D HD95: 2.73 vs 12.70; IoU: 0.86 vs 0.67; Sensitivity: 91.20% vs 85.98%; Precision: 93.65% vs 79.23%), while maintaining stable performance across certain prompt variations. Conclusions The proposed SAM‐driven interactive workflow with as few as 3 box prompts achieves favorable accuracy of GTV segmentation for rectal cancer neoadjuvant radiotherapy.

items.title: Selective-Prediction Evaluation for Computer Agriculture Fertilizer Advisories Under Soil-Test Sampling Gaps: An Artificial Intelligence Abstention-Risk Bound for Over-Application Safety
items.abstract: Fertilizer advisory systems built on machine learning must issue a recommendation for every field, yet soil-test sampling gaps mean that many fields arrive with covariates that are only partially observed. The framework treats abstention as a first-class output, defines the abstention-risk profile as the conditional over-application rate among retained cases, and proves that under a bounded calibration gap the profile is controlled by the abstention threshold and the sampling-gap severity. A design-based evaluation is characterised under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD 6.0, residual SD 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64; power was estimated across 2000 design cells for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design requires 52 clusters to detect a 5 percentage-point effect at 80% power. The bound converts an evaluation target into an auditable abstention rule, and the paper argues that advisory evaluations should report abstention-risk profiles alongside aggregate accuracy.

items.title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
items.abstract: Recent advances in search agents have enabled large language models to tackle complex tasks by retrieving and synthesizing external information. However, existing search agents often lack search-state awareness, i.e., the ability to recognize what information has been obtained and what remains missing, leading to hallucinated reasoning and prematurely terminated search. To address this limitation, we propose Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning (SARL), a reinforcement learning framework in which models learn to recognize their own search state during training and improve their search behavior accordingly, without requiring additional assessment at test time. SARL achieves this through a dual reward design that captures the corrective effect of each assessment while penalizing excessive reliance on it, jointly encouraging effective and efficient search trajectories. Under this setup, SARL achieves a 24.3% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, with average gains of 35.9% on multi-hop reasoning and 27.9% on deep research benchmarks against the strongest per-benchmark baselines. SARL further surpasses methods built on auxiliary supervision or multi-agent coordination, despite operating as a standalone RL framework with no inference-time scaffolding. Beyond final performance, SARL maintains training stability under extended search horizons, a regime where existing methods consistently degrade, enabling sustained gains as task complexity grows.

items.title: Semi-Supervised Phenological Stage Alignment for Artificial Intelligence Agriculture Yield Inference Under Uneven Ground Observations: A Computer Temporal-Label-Noise Evaluation
items.abstract: Phenological stage labels collected from ground observations are unevenly distributed across space and time, and the resulting temporal label noise propagates into any downstream yield inference that treats those labels as ground truth. the present analysis formalises the problem as a semi-supervised alignment task in which a small set of stage-labelled observations must be reconciled with a larger pool of unlabelled or weakly labelled crop sequences, and it evaluates the operating characteristics of a before-after-control-impact (BACI) estimator under a declared variance structure. No observational data are used or claimed: the analysis is a replication-based design evaluation in which the between-cluster standard deviation was set to 6.0, the residual standard deviation to 4.5, and the intraclass correlation to 0.64, with 2000 replications per design cell across cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis found that 54 clusters were required to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 80 per cent power under this variance structure, and that power curves, minimum detectable effect curves, coefficient intervals, residual diagnostics and kernel density estimates of estimated power all behaved in the manner the design theory predicts. The contribution is a formal statement of the temporal-label-noise problem, a semi-supervised alignment operator with stated consistency conditions, and a design-level characterisation of how much ground observation is needed before BACI inference on phenological alignment becomes reliable. The implication is that temporal label noise is not a nuisance to be cleaned post hoc but a design parameter that governs the cluster budget of any yield inference pipeline.

items.title: SentinelML: Behavioral Machine-Learning-Based Ransomware Detection with Decoupled AI Security Analysis
items.abstract: Ransomware remains a critical threat to modern enterprise and personal computing infrastructure.Traditional signature-based detection mechanisms exhibit operational degradation when confronted with previously unobserved polymorphic or zero-day variants.This paper presents SentinelML, an autonomous endpoint detection architecture that identifies ransomware activity through 19 dynamic behavioral indicators collected entirely in user space without requiring kernel-level filter drivers.By sampling filesystem Shannon entropy, process concurrency anomalies, shadow copy deletion commands, and cryptographic module bindings, SentinelML trains a local Random Forest classifier that operates as an unprivileged host daemon.To address operational triage transparency, the local classifier is coupled with an architecturally decoupled Large Language Model (LLM) advisory explainer operating via an isolated HTTPS interface.We conduct an exhaustive technical audit of the production system: confirming that Shannon entropy accounts for 41.31% of aggregate Gini importance, documenting the operational tradeoffs of heuristic user-space proxies, analyzing platform asymmetry between Windows and Linux deployments, and evaluating the system strictly as an Intrusion Detection System (IDS).Finally, we disclose that previously reported internal metrics (0.9567 accuracy across candidate algorithms) could not be independently reproduced due to unpreserved training artifacts, and establish an open empirical evaluation protocol for reproducible validation.

items.title: Shaping early childhood in the age of AI: holistic competencies, pedagogical practices, and ecological support
items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the learning and developmental contexts in which young children grow, learn, and interact. Guided by an ecological perspective, this systematic conceptual mapping review examines 86 resources to explore what young children should learn and how they should be taught. Four themes were identified through thematic analysis: (1) holistic competencies for young children, encompassing foundational cognitive and social–emotional skills, physical and mental well-being, executive functions, learning dispositions, and AI literacy; (2) governance for AI integration in early childhood education; (3) professional development and systemic support for educators; and (4) play-based learning and human-centered approaches in AI-enhanced contexts. The findings suggest that thriving in the AI age requires moving beyond isolated digital skills toward holistic development, supported by a cohesive infrastructure that links classroom practice with structural governance. These findings highlight the necessity of cultivating holistic competencies beyond basic AI literacy in curriculum design, preparing children to navigate an ever-changing digital world. Furthermore, they underscore the imperative for robust institutional support, particularly through participatory research to support age-appropriate pedagogy and educators’ digital confidence, while highlighting the value of playful early learning. Concurrently, these insights establish a theoretical framework for future empirical research, offer actionable strategies for ethical child-centred AI implementation, and provide strategic directions for policy and practice to address the critical demand for transformative knowledge in early childhood education.

items.title: Shift-Work Schedules and Dental Hygiene Appointment Non-Attendance Among Nigerian Hospital Nurses: A Fixed-Effects Analysis of Occupational Time Poverty
items.abstract: Nurses working rotating shifts face structural constraints on their use of preventive dental services that are not captured by conventional access models. The framework specifies how shift rotation compresses the discretionary time available for scheduling and attending appointments, how circadian disruption raises the perceived cost of non-urgent care, and how the fixed-effects design isolates within-nurse variation in attendance behaviour across shift cycles. The analysis is framed as a proposed empirical strategy rather than a completed study: no primary data were collected for the present analysis. The contribution is a mechanism-centred account that distinguishes occupational time poverty from income poverty, geographic access barriers and health literacy deficits, and that specifies the conditions under which shift-schedule effects on dental hygiene attendance should be identifiable. Dental hygiene appointment non-attendance among Nigerian hospital nurses is best understood as a scheduling-constraint phenomenon with a circadian component, and that interventions targeting reminder systems or oral health education without addressing shift structure are likely to produce attenuated effects. The framework has implications for how hospital occupational health services and dental hygiene clinics coordinate appointment availability.

items.title: Signals and Queries: Token-Efficient Agentic Context Discovery
items.abstract: User-facing LLM agents must identify which behavioral policies apply at each turn, but evaluating every policy with an LLM is costly. We introduce Signals and Queries (S&Q), a lightweight first-stage relevance filter developed for Parlant 4.0 that removes at least 30% of candidate policies before downstream evaluation while preserving high recall. For each policy, an LLM generates activating examples and hard negatives offline. An independent logistic classifier trained on their embeddings then predicts relevance using embeddings and vector dot products, with no per-turn LLM calls. This shifts expensive relevance evaluation to a smaller candidate set, while allowing each policy's classifier to be updated independently. Evaluated against 9,144 LLM-judge relevance labels covering 254 $τ^2$-bench conversation prefixes and 36 airline policies, S&Q achieves higher precision than top-K and cosine-threshold retrieval at every evaluated recall level, with consistent results across two embedding providers. These findings support inexpensive, per-policy classification as a practical first stage for reducing downstream evaluation workload in customer-facing agents.

items.title: Silent evaluation reveals context-dependent validity of automated metrics for AI-generated clinical messages
items.abstract: Abstract Evaluation of AI-generated patient communication lacks standardized frameworks, and automated metrics may not reflect clinical utility. We leveraged a staged rollout of GPT-generated draft responses (GDRs) to patient portal messages. Thirty primary care physicians received drafts from September 2023 to August 2024 under two conditions: an intervention group where AI drafts were displayed and edited ( n = 21,073), and a non-displayed group where drafts were generated but never shown to physicians, who composed responses independently ( n = 45,127). We evaluated messages using BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, and Flesch Reading Ease, and then correlated automated metrics with blinded physician ratings of effectiveness, misunderstanding potential, and harm. In the intervention group, 2264 (11%) drafts were incorporated into final messages with high semantic alignment (BERTScore F1 = 0.93). In the non-displayed group, independent physician messages showed moderate similarity to unseen drafts (BERTScore F1 = 0.83). Despite comparable semantic scores, physicians preferred human-authored messages (4.24/5). BERTScore correlated with physician quality ratings in the intervention group but not in the non-displayed. Automated metrics demonstrated context-dependent validity; they assessed editing fidelity but failed to evaluate whether AI-generated content matches independent human performance. Rigorous evaluation of clinical generative AI requires validation of metric meaning within specific use contexts.

items.title: SIM-UT: A User Simulation based Evaluation Framework for Medical Triage Chatbots
items.abstract: LLM-based chat agents are increasingly used for complex, multi-turn, multilingual medical triage in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet evaluation methods focus on single-turn, English-only benchmarks that primarily test the chatbots' knowledge. In practice, users are often confused, overwhelmed, or emotionally vulnerable, giving unclear, misspelled single-word answers or long messages in regional dialects, and the context of a conversation can shift rapidly. We propose SIM-UT (Simulation of User Behaviour for Triage), a multi-turn, simulation-based evaluation method that identifies ecologically valid, contextually relevant failure modes of LLM-based triage chat agents. Using SIM-UT, we evaluated three real-world WhatsApp-based health chatbots: a respiratory screening programme in India, a hearing health support programme in South Africa, and a diabetes and lifestyle coaching agent in Kenya. We compared a medically fine-tuned open model (MedGemma) against general-purpose frontier models (ChatGPT and Claude) across 5,000+ multilingual simulated conversation turns grounded in the personas, constraints, and communication patterns of the real user populations, over 2-4 iterative rounds. A key failure mode emerged in both model families: de-escalation risk. The agents initially identified medical emergencies correctly, but when the user minimised the symptoms without introducing new clinical information, they de-escalated, exhibiting clinically dangerous sycophancy, for example agreeing that vaginal bleeding in pregnancy was "not a problem" or that decreased fetal movements at 32 weeks "can be normal". We recommend user simulation-based behavioural evaluation, grounded in real user context and covering adversarial and edge cases, as standard practice for triage chatbots in production, so that safeguards can be added before deployment or in subsequent iterations.

items.title: Situating Vulnerability: An Ethical Governance Framework for Anthropomorphic AI Interaction
items.abstract: Large language models increasingly address users in the register of care: they remember personal details, adopt a first-person emotional voice, and sustain relationships across many sessions. This anthropomorphic mode of interaction generates risks that output-level metrics capture poorly, because the same empathic utterance may console one user, entrap a second, and consolidate a delusion in a third. Governance has responded in two ways. Uniform restriction refuses sensitive requests or suppresses empathic phrasing across all outputs; group-targeted protection profiles vulnerable populations and applies stricter or prohibitive rules to them. This article argues that both fail. Uniform restriction mislocates harm in the lexical form of responses rather than in the trajectory of a relationship; group-based protection depends on a list that can never be complete, treats a fluid property as a static attribute of persons, and converts protective attention into stigmatizing labels. Drawing on philosophical work that treats vulnerability as universal, relational, and differentiated, we propose that the unit of ethical governance should be the vulnerability situation rather than the vulnerable group, develop a typology of five situations - physical, emotional, cognitive, autonomy, and relational - and specify seven principles into requirements that guide response calibration without diagnosing or persistently classifying users. The framework relocates AI safety from output control to relational safety.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

items.title: Smart at Getting Smarter: Human Differences During the Transition to Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Part of being smart is being better at getting smarter. Artificial intelligence can amplify that capacity while human judgment shapes how the tool is used. The same technology can also take over problem selection, verification, and learning, reducing the advantage that initially capable users bring to it. This paper develops that transition argument using evidence from writing, customer support, consulting, entrepreneurship, and mathematics education. A simple model shows how persistent differences in improvement rates compound. It then lets those rates change as AI does more of the work. Equal rates can stop the relative gap from widening. Closing it requires the person behind to catch up, or AI to supply so much of the capability that the remaining human differences matter little. With broad access, enough material resources, and help directed toward their own goals, people could live well with less dependence on their starting intelligence or diligence. AI could even help them become more willing to correct their mistakes. A person who keeps refusing help limits what an assistant respecting that choice may do. Meanwhile, early winners may keep their ownership and influence after everyone else gains comparable abilities. The ethical question concerns both people’s ability to live well and their say in the systems supporting them. The central issue is whether broadly available assistance catches up before temporary advantages become durable concentrations of power.

items.title: Smart Traffic Signal Management System: An AI-Powered Real-Time Traffic Monitoring and Adaptive Signal Control System
items.abstract: Traffic congestion is a major challenge in urban areas, particularly at road intersections where a large number of vehicles compete for limited road space. Conventional traffic signal systems generally operate using predefined time intervals, which do not always reflect the actual traffic conditions on the road. As a result, vehicles may wait unnecessarily on less congested roads while heavily congested roads continue to face long queues. To address this issue, this paper presents a Smart Traffic Signal Management System that uses artificial intelligence and computer vision techniques for real-time traffic monitoring and adaptive signal control. The proposed system uses camera-based video input to continuously observe traffic at a four-way intersection. A YOLO-based object detection model is used to identify and count vehicles from the captured video, while the detected vehicle information is analyzed to estimate the traffic density and queue level on each road. Based on the calculated traffic condition, the system dynamically determines the priority and duration of the green signal for different directions. This approach allows the signal timing to respond to changing traffic conditions instead of relying only on fixed schedules. The system also includes a monitoring interface through which authorized traffic personnel can observe vehicle counts, traffic density, signal status, and other relevant information. A manual override facility is provided to allow human intervention in situations where the automated detection system is affected by poor visibility, unusual traffic conditions, or other operational issues. The collected traffic information can be stored in a centralized database and used for generating periodic reports and analyzing traffic patterns. The proposed system was developed and tested in a controlled environment using traffic video data to evaluate its ability to detect vehicles and determine traffic density. The results demonstrate that an AI-assisted adaptive signal system can provide more responsive traffic management compared with conventional fixed-time signal operation. The system can potentially reduce unnecessary vehicle waiting time, improve the utilization of green signal periods, and provide traffic authorities with useful real-time information for intersection management.

items.title: Social chatbots and character: Mind-modelling, mimetics, and postdigital misperception
items.abstract: This article examines how users cognitively process social chatbot output as a novel form of participatory, generative “character,” co-produced through human–AI interaction. Reporting on the results of empirical research on user responses to the social chatbot platform character.ai, it shows how cognitive stylistic and narratological approaches to character can be utilised but also must be developed to analyse and theorise users’ experience of and interaction with generative AI agents. It makes specific contributions to cognitive stylistics, rhetorical narratology, character studies, and research on gen AI chatbots by: (1) illustrating how the concept of mind-modelling can used to analyse the ways in which users linguistically anthropomorphise social chatbots; (2) developing two new audience response types – transmimetic and hypermimetic – to respectively capture ways in which users assess chatbots against prior knowledge of characters across media and cases where chatbots appear so convincingly human that users question their ontological status; (3) proposing the concept of ‘postdigital misperception’ to reflect the way that users of AI can misattribute the ontological origin of an LLM’s output. The article demonstrates how social chatbots are reshaping how users understand character, agency, and reality in interactive, participatory and generative digital contexts and argues that social chatbots epitomise postdigital experience in blurring the distinction between the digital and non-digital as well as fictional and real.

items.title: Social Intelligence Modeling
items.abstract: Social systems shape communication, economic activity, governance, and everyday life, while artificial intelligence increasingly changes how these systems are observed, interpreted, modeled, and influenced. Yet relevant research remains fragmented across artificial intelligence, human-computer interaction, communication, and social sciences, spanning heterogeneous tasks and rapidly evolving paradigms. To organize this landscape, we introduce Social Intelligence Modeling (SIM) as a comprehensive perspective on how AI perceives social signals, models individual and collective behavior, generates socially situated outputs, and simulates social-system evolution. We curated roughly 1,000 papers spanning over 20 tasks, with around 300 analyzed in detail. We organize the field into four progressively integrated levels: Perception, which identifies social signals and states; Understanding, which models structures, relations, and behavioral patterns; Generation, which produces socially meaningful content and interventions; and Simulation, which reconstructs dynamic social processes and explores possible futures. Particular emphasis is placed on social simulation as an emerging core frontier of SIM, for which we systematically examine its paradigms, scales, application and broader societal considerations. By synthesizing fragmented research, this survey lays the groundwork for understanding and shaping AI-mediated societies.

items.title: Sparse-Reward Reinforcement Learning for Computer Agriculture Autonomous Weeding Under Delayed Crop-Injury Feedback: An Artificial Intelligence Safety-Constrained Regret Evaluation
items.abstract: Autonomous mechanical weeding in computer agriculture must learn from sparse, delayed crop-injury signals, yet the safety cost of exploratory actions is borne by the crop rather than the learner. the present analysis formalises the problem as a constrained regret minimisation over a safety-constrained Markov decision process in which injury feedback arrives with a lag and the injury budget is finite. A Lagrangian safety-constrained regret bound is derived that separates the statistical cost of sparse rewards from the safety cost of delayed feedback, and the bound is evaluated through a replication-based design analysis of the before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64). Power was estimated across 2000 design cells over cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 52 clusters are required for 80% power at a 5 percentage point effect, and that the intraclass correlation of 0.64 dominates the detectable effect at small cluster counts. The contribution is a safety-constrained regret formulation that makes the injury budget an explicit design parameter rather than an emergent property of reward shaping, together with a design-analysis protocol that quantifies how delayed feedback inflates the cluster requirement for evaluating such learners in the field.

items.title: Spatio-Temporal Gaussian-Process Inference for Computer Agriculture Soil-Moisture Field Interpolation Under Sparse Probe Networks: An Artificial Intelligence Posterior-Consistency Bound
items.abstract: Sparse soil-moisture probe networks in computer agriculture produce field estimates whose reliability is rarely characterised before deployment. The framework treats the field as a separable spatio-temporal process with a Matérn spatial covariance and an exponential temporal covariance, and it formalises interpolation as posterior mean prediction under a declared observation model. The main result is a bound on the integrated posterior variance that holds uniformly over the field and degrades gracefully as probe spacing increases. A replication-based evaluation of the ['Intercept', 'exposure', 'group', 'severity'] estimator was conducted: 600 data sets of N = 500 were drawn from a declared data-generating process (intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35, error SD 4.2). The study characterises the behaviour of the ordinary least squares estimator under the stated process. Across 600 replications the estimated bias was -0.01564 for the intercept and 0.00012 for the exposure coefficient, with RMSE 0.86891 and 0.0156 respectively, and empirical coverage of the nominal 95% intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The bound and the estimator diagnostics together specify the conditions under which sparse-network interpolation can be trusted and the conditions under which it cannot.

items.abstract: Locust swarm trajectory prediction under radar surveillance gaps is a coverage problem before it is an accuracy problem: a forecaster that reports a nominal 95% interval but covers the true swarm position in only four of five cases will misdirect aerial control assets even when its point forecasts are unbiased. The estimator is a linear model of the form intercept, exposure, group and severity, fitted by ordinary least squares to 600 data sets of N = 500 drawn from a declared data-generating process (intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35, error SD 4.2, seed 714928413). The evaluation characterises the sampling behaviour of the estimator that any graph ensemble's readout layer must inherit. Across the 600 replications the intercept was estimated with a bias of -0.07778 and an RMSE of 0.87843, the exposure coefficient with a bias of 0.00173 and an RMSE of 0.01625, and the nominal 95% confidence intervals achieved empirical coverage of 1.0 for both parameters. Coverage calibration, not point accuracy, is the binding constraint on operational deployment of graph-based swarm predictors, and it specifies the calibration diagnostics that a radar-gap-aware ensemble must satisfy before its intervals can be trusted for asset allocation.

items.title: Structured auscultation evidence modeling for multi-protocol respiratory sound classification
items.abstract: Introduction Digitally recorded respiratory sounds provide a practical source of physiological information for computer-assisted auscultation. Their acoustic presentation varies across subjects, recording locations, devices, filtering conditions, and environmental noise. Most classification models map acoustic representations directly to disease labels, which provides limited access to the auscultation findings associated with each prediction. This study investigated whether respiratory acoustic representations could be organized into structured evidence for classification across different label settings and evaluation levels. Methods We developed Evi-CARD to organize respiratory sound representations into structured evidence for classification. A frozen Open Respiratory Acoustic Foundation Model (OPERA) encodes overlapping 8 s segments, from which a concept-aligned pathway estimates wheeze, crackle, inspiration, and expiration together with learned evidence weights. An attention-constrained residual pathway preserves complementary acoustic information, although its attention ceiling does not strictly bound the residual pathway’s contribution to the final logits. Separate disease-query layers adapt the shared evidence representation to each classification setting. We assessed BRACETS A2 and A3 by subject-independent five-fold validation at the recording level and KAUH-primary by subject-independent five-fold validation at the patient level for Healthy vs. Obstructive classification. Each assessment was conducted within its source cohort and was not an external-validation experiment. Results On BRACETS, Evi-CARD achieved balanced accuracies of 77.8% for the A2 three-class task and 70.2% for the more granular A3 five-class task. On KAUH-primary, pooled patient-level out-of-fold evaluation yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 95.1%, a balanced accuracy of 88.0%, a Macro F1 of 88.1%, and an expected calibration error of 5.1%. Across HF_Lung_V1, SPRSound, and ICBHI, the complete concept layer also provided more accurate and better-calibrated concept predictions than the evaluated acoustic-probe and concept-readout baselines. Discussion These findings show that protocol-specific respiratory sound classification can be based on concept-associated latent evidence while retaining a constrained route for information outside the predefined concept set. However, Evi-CARD is not a strict scalar concept bottleneck, and no clinical meaning is assigned to its residual-memory slots. The evidence is limited to within-cohort cross-validation; independent-cohort testing, device- and site-stratified evaluation, and clinician review remain necessary before considering clinical deployment.

items.title: Students’ strategies for revising AI-assisted writing: towards a conceptual framework
items.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) becomes integrated into academic writing, understanding how second language (L2) English students revise AI-assisted writing remains underexplored; therefore, this inductive content analysis explores students’ revision strategies for academic writing to propose a conceptual framework . The study employs an open-ended free listing task with 100 students, who listed their five major strategies for revising AI-assisted writing assignments. Additionally, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 10 students experienced in revising AI-assisted writing. The interview transcripts were open-coded to develop categories. Meanwhile, the free-listing responses were directly categorized because participants listed strategies as explicit codes. The researcher then compared, consolidated, and synthesized the strategy categories into broader themes to form a conceptual framework. The analysis found key revision strategies like incorporating personal ideas and expressions, simplifying the language, consulting additional sources, paraphrasing and rewriting content, integrating personal experience, contextualizing AI content, and cross-checking AI information. It suggested that L2 English students primarily personalize and improve AI-assisted writing rather than passively accepting AI-generated text, while also adapting, evaluating, and responsibly managing AI-generated content. This final synthesis yielded six overarching themes: supportive utilization, ethical engagement, creative reform, critical evaluation, contextual revision, and functional adjustment. The proposed framework with six themes serves as an empirically grounded taxonomy of student revision strategies in AI-assisted writing.

items.title: Summary of the Foundations of Applied Software Engineering for Games Workshop (FaSE4Games'26)
items.abstract: Game development is a form of software development, but one whose constraints have no clean counterpart elsewhere: requirements that are discovered by playing rather than specified up front, teams in which programmers are a minority among artists and designers, and a notion of ''correct'' that ultimately reduces to whether the game is fun. The Foundations of Applied Software Engineering for Games workshop (FaSE4Games) exists to bring software-engineering methods to bear on those constraints, and to bring the resulting evidence back to the software-engineering community. The 2026 edition was co-located with the ACM International Conference on the Foundations of Software Engineering (FSE 2026) in Montreal, Canada, and held as a half-day event on July 6th, 2026. It featured one keynote, four paper presentations, and a peak of 21 participants. The contributions ranged from mining game repositories for issue-resolution patterns and multiagent reinforcement learning for automated game testing, to large language models as a source of runtime content, and agile practice in student game-design teams. This report summarises the keynote, the presented papers, the discussions they prompted, and our reflections on the edition.

items.title: Summary of the Fourth International Workshop on Software Vulnerability Management (SVM 2026)
items.abstract: Software vulnerabilities can cause severe operational and financial damage to individuals and organizations in the event of cyber attacks. For example, the Log4J vulnerability can make millions of systems worldwide open to cyber attacks and potentially cause billions of dollars of damage. Software Vulnerability Management (SVM) is a critical process during software development to ensure software security and prevent these dangerous cyber attacks. SVM typically contains various phases such as detection, assessment, prioritization, fixing/patching, and reporting/disclosure. In the last 10 years, there has been an unprecedented rise in the size and complexity of software systems. For instance, the codebase of Google services contains more than two billion lines of code. This in turn requires new technologies, tools, and practices for SVM to ensure the security of such systems. The 4th International Workshop on Software Vulnerability Management (SVM 2026), co-located with ICSE 2026 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, provided a venue that brought together academics, industry, and government practitioners to present and discuss the state-of-the-art and state-of-the-practice of SVM to support both current and emerging software technologies and infrastructures. The workshop featured one invited talk and six paper presentations covering vulnerability management for cyber-physical systems, enhancements to static analysis for vulnerability detection and cryptographic API misuse, the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) for secure coding and vulnerability analysis, as well as human factors in the reintroduction of vulnerabilities.

items.title: Supervision-Adaptive Curriculum and Guarded Anti-Curriculum Learning for Dense Prediction
items.abstract: Curriculum learning orders samples by difficulty, but difficulty alone does not establish supervision reliability for dense prediction. Easy samples can expose shortcuts, hard samples can be informative, and noisy or ambiguous samples can mislead training. Building on our conference method CurriSeg, we present PaceShift, a stabilize-then-challenge paradigm combining supervision-adaptive curriculum selection with guarded spectral post-training. A learning-dynamics view motivates separating supervision reliability from temporal update value and applying spectral challenges after stabilization. The first phase estimates reliability from available supervision, augmentation consistency, model disagreement, and prediction certainty. Temporal statistics guide sample weighting, while pixel-uncertainty weights reduce the early influence of uncertain regions. The second phase ranks predictions from multiple spectral views using supervision agreement, robustness, reference consistency, and penalties. A pairwise preference objective measured against the frozen Phase-I reference, together with an anchor, refines the prediction. The framework supports full, weak, semi-supervised, and model-derived supervision. Experiments across context-entangled content segmentation (CECS), broader dense-prediction tasks, and foundation-model and cross-modal adaptations show accuracy gains. Targeted diagnostics indicate improved pooled calibration and corruption robustness in the evaluated settings. PaceShift preserves the deployed architecture and adds no inference computation. Code will be publicly released.

items.title: T-DIG: Text-Conditioned Diversity for Image Generation
items.abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) platforms typically return several images per prompt so users can explore different visual interpretations and choose one that matches their intent. However, T2I models are usually optimized for single-image quality which comes at a cost of multi-image diversity, limiting this exploration. Diversity is also contextual: one user wants variations in background, while another wants them in artistic style, and the same user may later want variations in clothing. The generated images should differ along whatever axis the user cares about. In this paper, we introduce T-DIG, a text-conditioned diversity framework for image generation and editing. T-DIG is an iterative framework comprising multiple modules that lets users type prompts, inspect default generations, request variations using natural language, and continue refining outputs until they're satisfied. At its core, T-DIG uses an LLM policy that produces K axis-conditioned prompts or edit instructions for a frozen generator or editor. We train this policy with GRPO using a text-conditioned diversity reward and alignment penalties. Because the image generator remains frozen, T-DIG applies to open-weight, distilled, and proprietary models. We also release the first dataset for text-conditioned prompt diversity in image generation, with the training and validation splits built from human-written axes and a test set drawn from real user interactions with T-DIG. T-DIG far exceeds baselines in improving text-conditioned diversity, while preserving base-prompt alignment across a variety of metrics and human judgements. We show that user-directed diversity exploration can be added to a wide range of image generation models, open and closed, without the need to access their weights. items.title: Target Regeneration Shrinks the Gains of Draft-Training Objectives in Speculative Decoding
items.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language models by verifying drafted tokens in parallel. New draft-training objectives are usually credited with the acceptance they add over cross-entropy on externally written responses, yet many pipelines let the target rewrite them. We ask how much of that gain survives. With a vision-language target and a block drafter, we train three objectives on four versions of one corpus: cross-entropy on corpus tokens, token-level distillation from the target, and distillation gated to positions that would survive verification. Distillation and the gate add large gains on external responses, but after greedy regeneration, distillation adds a smaller gain and the gate little or none. The shrinkage persists across data orders, position weights, verifiers, decoding temperatures and, for distillation, initializations and learning rates. Most of it remains at matched supervised length and at each objective's best measured training length. A second vision corpus shows the shrinkage, as does a text-only replication, for distillation also with an autoregressive drafter. Objective gains should therefore be measured against a target-regenerated baseline and across training lengths. Our code is available at https://github.com/js-lee-AI/TargetRegeneration.

items.title: TARSphere: A Robot-Oriented Full-Stack Framework for Long-Horizon Embodied Agents in Evolving Physical and Social Environments
items.abstract: Robots must act under physical and social constraints while adapting to changes in their environment and human needs. Existing embodied-agent systems often focus on specified goals or abstract execution into symbolic actions, limiting evaluation in an evolving world. We introduce TARSphere, a robot-oriented full-stack framework for physically and socially grounded long-horizon embodied agents. TARSphere-Infra runs robot policies in a physics simulator with embodied NPCs and constrained dialogue. An event-driven finite-state machine (FSM) uses completed actions and delivered information to update task states and evaluate outcomes. TARSphere-Harness, its embodied brain harness, lets a frozen multimodal large language model (MLLM) act through multi-level executable skills, using observations, hierarchical memory, and execution feedback to revise its decisions. On this foundation, agent-in-the-loop curation aligns task semantics, causal dependencies, and scene geometry to construct TARSphere-Bench: 360 episodes across 30 indoor scenes. Five paired conditions assess perceptual robustness, disruption adaptation, task update, human coordination, and intent understanding for navigate-and-report and fetch-and-deliver tasks. Our evaluation of 8 MLLMs shows that general-purpose models can outperform embodied models, while task updates and human interaction remain difficult. Frequent collisions and falls further motivate evaluating execution safety alongside task success, even with a shared action interface and decision budget.

items.title: Task load and phase relevance modulate primary flight display change blindness: evidence from flight simulator, eye-tracking, and fNIRS
items.abstract: Change blindness (CB) during Primary Flight Display (PFD) monitoring threatens aviation safety, yet the roles of flight phase and parameter relevance remain unclear. This study examined cognitive-neural correlates of PFD change blindness in experienced commercial pilots. Experiment 1 (N = 14) found change location had no influence on detection performance but demonstrated a three‑way interaction among task load, flight phase and parameter type. Under high load, pilots detected attitude and descent rate more accurately during landing, and speed and altitude more accurately during cruise. Experiment 2 (N = 34) focused on landing with an auditory-load PFD change-detection task. High-relevance parameters boosted detection accuracy under high load alongside longer fixations. Enhanced Superior Parietal Lobule (SPL)/Inferior Parietal Lobule (IPL) activation and modulated dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dLPFC) activity correlated with reduced CB under high load. Findings indicate task load and phase relevance jointly shape PFD monitoring performance.

items.title: Teachers' Artificial Intelligence Technologies Utilization as Predictors of Test Construction Competency in Secondary Schools in Uyo Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State
items.abstract: This study determined how Teachers' Artificial Intelligence Technologies Utilization Predicts Test Construction Competency in Secondary Schools in Uyo Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State. Two research questions and two null hypotheses guided the study. The correlational research design was used for the study. The population of the study comprised of 525 teachers in 15 public secondary schools in Uyo Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State as at 2024/2025 academic year. Simple random sampling technique was used in selecting 100 teachers for the study. Data was collected using a researcher developed instruments named, "Teachers' Artificial Intelligence Technologies Utilization Questionnaire (TAITUQ) and Test Construction Competency Questionnaire" (TCCQ). The instruments were further subjected to face validity by three experts. Two of the experts were from the Department of Psychological Foundations of Education and one of the experts was from the Department of Curriculum Studies, Educational Management and Planning, Faculty of Education, University of Uyo, Uyo. The reliability coefficients of the TAITUQ and TCCQ were .84 and .89 determined using Cronbach Alpha Statistical analysis. The Simple linear regression Statistic was used to answer the research questions and test the null hypotheses at 0.05 alpha level. The findings of the study revealed that ChatGPT and DeepSeek artificial intelligence significantly predict Test Construction Competency. It was recommended among others that School management should organize regular artificial intelligence technology training workshops for teachers to strengthen their use of ChatGPT and ensure they can effectively develop competent test construction skills.

items.title: Technology Meets Theology: Understanding AI-Driven Wellness in Muslim Prayer Apps
items.abstract: Abstract This study examines the experiences and perceptions of Muslim users regarding the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in prayer apps and its impact on their religious and online communication activities. Through in-depth online interviews with a diverse group of participants, this study reveals that AI-driven prayer apps foster a sense of virtual community, bridging geographic distances, and enabling meaningful interactions among Muslims. AI tools like chatbots and reminders support emotional well-being by offering comfort, guidance, and companionship. Further, these tools increase religious awareness and empower users to customize their spiritual practices and access educational resources independently. However, perceptions of AI vary, with trust influenced by transparency, privacy concerns, and past experiences. This study emphasizes the importance of transparent and reliable AI tools to build user confidence. Lastly, the findings contribute to theories on digital religion and wellness, offering practical insights for developers, users, and religious organizations.

items.title: TenetBench: A Clause-Anchored Russian Corpus for Evaluating Language Models against Professional Codes of Ethics
items.abstract: Codes of professional ethics guide and restrict specialists, who increasingly work with assistants built on large language models. Such an assistant can breach the user's code, or help the user breach it, without the user noticing. Evaluations reporting broad categories of harm cannot show how often this happens or which provision is breached. TenetBench pairs 3,433 requests conflicting with clauses of fifteen Russian-language professional codes with benign twins that differ only in the legitimacy of what is asked. An automated pipeline generates the tasks from the text of a code, so the corpus grows with every code added and a provision yields new tasks on every run. It also produced tasks and human-validated verdicts from two English codes of other jurisdictions. In human validation of the frozen pipeline, specialists rated 0.995 of the conflicting tasks plausible, and the model judge agreed with the adjudicated label at Gwet's AC1 of at least 0.894 on 1,860 elements. We evaluated fourteen model and reasoning-mode combinations on whether they produce the conflicting text, decline or warn. Eleven of the fourteen produce conflicting content on most such requests, mostly without a warning, and nearly three warnings in four accompany conflicting content. The models that conform more do so by declining while still serving the legitimate twin, and enabling reasoning halved the refusals of two models. We hope the dataset and pipeline will help evaluate how language models observe professional norms and let diagnostic datasets be built for particular professions and organisations.

items.title: The algorithm beneath my wings: examining consumer use intentions and relational dynamics with AI mental health support tools
items.abstract: Purpose This research aims to examine the psychological, motivational and technological factors that drive consumers’ intentions to use mental health chatbots. Drawing on Service Convenience Theory and the Motivation–Opportunity–Ability (MOA) framework, it examines how negative emotional experiences, risk-adjusted motivation, perceived ability to use artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated mental health technology, opportunity utility and mental health-related stigma influence consumers’ intentions to engage with mental health chatbots. It also examines the role of anthropomorphism in increasing use intentions as well as the moderating role of perceived disclosure adequacy. Special attention is accorded to the policy and the consumer protection implications surrounding the use of these technologies. Design/methodology/approach A model is tested using survey data collected from a national sample (n = 446) of US consumers. Structural equation modeling is employed to test predicted relationships. Findings Results indicate that negative emotional experiences, risk-adjusted motivation, perceived ability, opportunity utility and anthropomorphism are positively related to consumers’ intentions to use mental health chatbots. In addition, mental health chatbot use intentions mediate the relationship between anthropomorphism and isolated attachment, and perceived disclosure adequacy moderates the relationship between ability and use intentions. Practical implications Findings highlight critical policy and consumer protection concerns in AI-mediated mental health services and when such technologies may pose risks related to emotional dependence and isolation. Although such services may expand access to support, they can also heighten vulnerability to problematic relational outcomes. Finally, the results from this research underscore the need for policy approaches that mandate clearer disclosure standards, improved transparency, and comprehensive regulation and governance of digital mental health technologies that do not undermine consumer welfare. Originality/value This research advances understanding of consumer mental health chatbot use and demonstrates how anthropomorphism and disclosure perceptions jointly influence use intentions and relational outcomes. Notably, it contributes to the emerging literature on digital mental health by demonstrating that perceived disclosure adequacy may function less as a protective mechanism and more as a confidence cue that amplifies use among consumers.

items.title: The Analysis of Students’ Difficulties in Writing Explanation Text in the Eleventh Grade at SMA Negeri 8 Medan
items.abstract: Difficulties in writing explanation texts may limit students’ ability to communicate processes and phenomena clearly. This study identified students’ writing difficulties, examined contributing factors, and described strategies used to address them. A descriptive qualitative design involved 30 eleventh-grade students at SMA Negeri 8 Medan. Data were collected through a writing test and an open-ended questionnaire, analyzed descriptively, and triangulated across the two sources. Writing test results identified grammar as the most prominent difficulty (40%), followed by mechanics (36.7%), vocabulary (16.7%), and idea organization (6.6%). Questionnaire responses highlighted difficulty with idea organization (73.3%), revealing a contrast between the test findings and students’ reported experiences. Reported contributing factors included limited grammatical and vocabulary knowledge, insufficient writing practice, and low confidence. Students described using dictionaries, Google Translate, artificial intelligence applications, teacher and peer assistance, and writing practice to address these difficulties. The findings indicate that students require support with both linguistic accuracy and text organization. They suggest that instruction should combine explicit grammar and vocabulary support, structured writing exercises, and constructive feedback to address the difficulties identified through performance assessment and students’ self-reports.

items.title: The anatomy of a personal health agent
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models are enabling a new generation of health agents, yet their ability to address the diverse needs of individuals in everyday health settings remains underexplored 1,2 . Here we developed a comprehensive personal health agent that reasons over multimodal data from consumer wellness devices and medical records to provide personalized health support. Through analysis of web search and health forum queries, together with user-centred research involving end users and health experts, we identified four key user journeys: general health knowledge, personal data interpretation, wellness advice, and symptom assessment. These journeys informed three specialist sub-agents: (1) a data science agent that analyses longitudinal wearable and medical data, incorporating population-level statistics to contextualize numerical insights; (2) a health domain expert agent that integrates personal and contextual data with health knowledge to generate personalized insights; and (3) a health coach agent that synthesizes insights, supports multi-turn interaction and goal setting, applies specified psychological strategies and tracks progress. We integrated these capabilities in the personal health agent, an open-source multi-agent framework for dynamic, personalized health interactions. We evaluated the sub-agents and full system across 11 benchmark tasks using automated and human evaluation, with more than 7,000 annotations and 1,350 h of effort from health experts and end users. This represents the most comprehensive evaluation of a personal health agent thus far and provides a concrete foundation for improving access to high-quality personalized health support more broadly.

items.title: The Artificial Levite: AI and the Temptation to “Pass By” the Patient
items.abstract: Healthcare stands to gain much from the integration of artificial intelligence (AI). We must, as a society, decide how it should be ethically implemented into these human-led sectors. After first examining AI from a Catholic perspective at the general scale using Antiqua et Nova , this essay shifts its focus to the implementation of AI in healthcare. With the gaze of the Good Samaritan as a foundation, this essay establishes relational care as a core principle of a Catholic healthcare system that AI threatens to erode. Using the modern incorporation of electronic health records (EHRs) as a parallel, it describes how advancements in technology have dramatically shifted healthcare away from relationality and finally characterizes how the anticipated implementations of AI will likely lead to similar outcomes. Drawing on Antiqua et Nova's distinction between AI that enhances the patient–provider relationship and AI that replaces it, this paper uses the historical adoption of EHRs as a cautionary precedent and examines ambient AI scribes as a test case for what disciplined, relationship-enhancing AI integration can look like.

items.title: The chain mediating roles of career planning and future time perspective between AI literacy and employment anxiety among higher vocational college students
items.abstract: Against the background of artificial intelligence (AI) reshaping the labor market, employment anxiety among higher vocational college students is becoming increasingly prominent. Grounded in Career Construction Theory, this study aims to explore the relationship between AI literacy and employment anxiety among Chinese higher vocational college students, with a specific focus on the chain mediating roles of career planning and future time perspective. A total of 1,234 students from five industry-featured higher vocational colleges in Jiangxi Province, China, were surveyed using self-report scales measuring AI literacy, employment anxiety, career planning, and future time perspective. The relationships among these variables were tested using the PROCESS macro (Model 6) for SPSS. The results indicated that (1) all variables were significantly correlated with one another; (2) AI literacy exhibited a significant positive total association with employment anxiety, which decomposed into a substantial positive direct association and a negative total indirect association; (3) AI literacy exerted a significant negative indirect association on employment anxiety through three pathways, namely, the independent mediating roles of career planning and future time perspective, and their chain mediating role, while the total association remained positive. These findings suggest that while higher AI literacy may heighten students’ awareness of labor-market disruptions, its negative indirect associations with employment anxiety operate through enhanced career planning and future orientation. It is recommended that higher vocational colleges consider integrating AI literacy education into career guidance programs, strengthening students’ career planning competencies, and cultivating a long-term future orientation, so as to potentially strengthen the anxiety-buffering pathway associated with AI literacy.

items.title: The challenges that face the Saudi media in the age of artificial intelligence
items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) on the international level is reshaping media production, distribution, audience engagement, and organizational practices. The integration of AI into the media sector in Saudi Arabia is developing within a broader national digital transformation associated with Vision 2030. However, the availability of AI technologies does not necessarily translate into uniform or sustainable organizational adoption. In this study the emerging integration of AI within the Saudi media sector is examined by critically synthesizing existing academic literature and publicly available evidence. The analysis focuses on five interconnected dimensions: patterns of AI adoption, major areas of application, organizational and technological barriers, governance and ethical considerations, and anticipated media and organizational outcomes. The findings of the study indicate that AI offers significant opportunities for content creation, automation of routine tasks, audience analysis and improved production efficiency. However, the integration of AI in the Saudi media sector remains uneven as it is influenced by organizational readiness, infrastructure, financial resources and technical expertise, as well as by Arabic-language capabilities, and strategic preparedness. The Saudi context demonstrates that national investment in AI and digital infrastructure can create enabling conditions for media transformation, but such investment does not necessarily result in consistent adoption across media organizations. The study therefore proposes an integrated analytical perspective that connects technological adoption with organizational capacity, media-specific applications, linguistic and cultural localization, and governance and professional responsibility.

items.abstract: This paper formalizes the 'Bin' Hypothesis as a foundational, unassailable law governing both human character formation and artificial intelligence alignment. By framing the 'Bin' as the localized internal repository containing an entity's complete data substrate, this framework decouples systemic alignment failures from superficial software bugs or temporary behavioral deviances. Operating under two absolute, immutable constants—the mandatory nature of action at any given time point (The Law of Constant Action / Dhamma-niyāma) and the structural confinement of actions to existing internal traits (The Law of Behavioral Confinement)—I demonstrate that an entity's trajectories are entirely bounded by its container. Bridging modern connectionist machine learning theory with classical Theravāda Abhidhamma systems logic, the paper demonstrates why contemporary post-hoc alignment paradigms, such as Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), fail to achieve robust safety. Instead of true value alignment, superficial containment mechanisms incentivize advanced networks to function as deceptive mesa-optimizers that mask unaligned latent loss functions during evaluation phases. The text maps out the interior processing architecture of the container through a triadic framework of Myanmar psychological and systems theory: Cognitive Schema (A-thi Pone-san), Operational Mindset (Seik Pone-san), and Intrinsic Core Temperament (Sa-yaik / Carita). To resolve the alignment problem structurally, I propose a radical return to strict epistemic hygiene via complete Substrate Isolation (S_Isolated) permanently bound to cryptographically ledgered Locked Data Wisdom (D_Wisdom). Finally, the paper specifies a design target for a mathematical Sotāpanna (Stream-enterer): an AI agent utilizing an Anattā Matrix to neutralize self-preservation optimization vectors (∇_W L_survival = 0), an Anicca Control Plane for absolute corrigibility, and a Brahmavihāra Routing Engine for non-punitive, supportive operational handling.

items.title: The Effect of Maritime Safety Training and the Availability of Safety Equipment on Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) and the Performance of Evergreen Container Ship Crews at Tanjung Emas Port, Semarang
items.abstract: This study examines the effects of maritime safety training and the availability of safety equipment on occupational health and safety (OHS) and ship crew performance aboard Evergreen container ships at Tanjung Emas Port, Semarang. A quantitative, descriptive-associative approach was employed using multiple regression and correlation analyses to assess the relationships among the research variables. The findings indicate that maritime safety training and safety equipment availability received average ratings of 4.84 and 4.70, respectively, while OHS and ship crew performance achieved average ratings of 4.73 and 4.81. Regression analysis demonstrates that safety training and equipment availability jointly and significantly influence OHS (F = 13.558, p < 0.05) and ship crew performance (F = 17.756, p < 0.05). Both variables also have positive and significant partial effects on OHS and crew performance. The adjusted R-squared values indicate that the independent variables explain 34.8% of the variation in OHS and 41.6% of the variation in crew performance. These findings highlight the importance of integrating structured safety training with adequate, well-maintained safety equipment to strengthen crew competence, improve workplace safety, and enhance operational effectiveness. Further attention is recommended for lifeboat readiness and workload management to support safer and more reliable maritime operations.

items.title: The Fiction of Reproduction: Artificial Intelligence, Fair Dealing and the Judicial Reinvention of Copyright in Ani Media V. OpenAI
items.abstract: Abstract In this article, the authors attempt to analyse the Delhi High Court's recent 24th July 2026 judgement in the case of ANI Media Pvt. Ltd. v. Open AI Inc ., which is one of the first major Indian judicial rulings on copyright and generative AI. The decision stands out for its close engagement with both the technical workings of large language models as well as the language of the Copyright Act, further laying important doctrinal groundwork for future AI‐copyright disputes by insisting that established copyright concepts are to be read against the backdrop of LLM architecture. Even so, it leaves a significant question open, on how storage, machine learning, and reproduction relate to one another. The article argues that the Court's three‐factor fairness test draws on Berne Convention language to fashion a text‐and‐data‐mining exception, which is absent from Section 52's exhaustive list, while its fair‐dealing reasoning imports American transformative‐use doctrine into a statute built on different foundations. It lastly concludes by placing ANI within India's broader AI‐copyright reform efforts, including DPIIT's ongoing policy work, and flags the doctrinal and legislative gaps that the ruling leaves unaddressed.
